name: Abbott
description: Abbott is a diversified health-care maker with four reported segments. Medical Devices (48 percent of 2025 sales, 61 percent of segment operating earnings) is the engine: heart devices plus the FreeStyle Libre continuous glucose monitor, which alone was $8.0B in 2025 (Diabetes Care). Diagnostics sells lab instruments and the tests (reagents) that run on them, plus rapid tests, and is shrinking as COVID test demand fades. Nutritionals sells infant formula (Similac) and adult drinks (Ensure, Glucerna, Pedialyte). Established Pharmaceuticals sells branded generic medicines only outside the US, mostly in emerging markets. In March 2026 Abbott closed the roughly $20.6B acquisition of Exact Sciences and now reports cancer diagnostics (Exact's tests) inside Diagnostics.

sub.name: Surgical and hospital devices and diagnostics

gics.note: SEC SIC code is 2834 (Pharmaceutical Preparations). Medical Devices is 48% of sales; the other 52% is branded generics, infant formula and diagnostics, so no single box describes the company.

businessLines.name: Medical Devices
businessLines.shareBasis: Share of revenue = 21,387 / 44,328 total net sales. Share of profit = 7,212 / 11,800 total segment operating earnings.
businessLines.how: Hospitals and physicians buy implanted devices and catheters one procedure at a time (volume follows procedure counts), while FreeStyle Libre is sold as sensors plus data-management software, accessories and test strips (10-K), a consumable that is bought again and again. Who pays (pharmacy, insurer, consumer) was not extracted.
businessLines.description: Rhythm management (pacemakers including Aveir leadless, defibrillators), electrophysiology (ablation catheters, mapping), heart failure (HeartMate, CardioMEMS), vascular (XIENCE stents, closure devices), structural heart (MitraClip, TriClip, Navitor), neuromodulation, and Diabetes Care (FreeStyle Libre and the Lingo consumer CGM).

operatingProfit.note: Segment operating earnings before corporate costs, amortization, share-based comp and interest; FY2024 $6,153M; H1 2026 $3,862M

businessLines.name: Diagnostics
businessLines.how: Labs and hospitals place an instrument and then buy the reagents and consumables that run on it, so revenue recurs with test volume; rapid tests are sold per kit to retailers, governments and clinics, which is why COVID demand swings the total. Cancer Diagnostics (Exact Sciences) revenue model was not described in the filings read.
businessLines.description: Core laboratory instruments and tests (Alinity, ARCHITECT), molecular PCR, point-of-care (i-STAT), rapid tests (BinaxNOW, ID NOW), informatics, and since March 2026 Cancer Diagnostics from Exact Sciences.

businessLines.name: Nutritionals
businessLines.how: Consumers buy infant formula and adult drinks repeatedly at retail; the segment also sells feeding products to hospitals and to government programs. Revenue follows birth-rate-driven volume, market share and price.
businessLines.description: Infant and pediatric formula (Similac, EleCare, Gain, Grow), adult nutrition (Ensure, Glucerna, PediaSure, Pedialyte) and enteral feeding products for hospitals.

businessLines.how: Country-by-country sales of branded generic drugs directly to wholesalers, distributors, pharmacies and government agencies; revenue grows with prescriptions and price in emerging markets and is exposed to currency.
